title: Quranic Audio Dataset: Crowdsourced and Labeled Recitation from Non-Arabic Speakers
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not benchmark a model, but creates a dataset to enable the development and benchmarking of AI models that measure the correctness of Quranic recitation by non-Arabic speakers. The annotation process measures recitation correctness against standard Arabic pronunciation and diacritics.
findings: The study found that beginner Muslim learners are willing to crowdsource their Quranic recitation recordings (7000 collected), but proficient reciters are more hesitant to participate in annotating this religious data. A crowdsourcing platform was successfully developed to label the recitations, achieving a crowd accuracy of 0.77 and an inter-rater agreement of 0.63. The label aggregation algorithm showed a high accuracy (0.94) and strong agreement with expert judgments (0.89), demonstrating the feasibility of creating a labeled dataset for this religious practice.
